levels.claim: one thing a reviewer said, identified by its finding_key (`file::summary`). Counted as `distinct_finding_keys`
levels.label: one judgement written to disk about one claim — one file per (arm, finding_key). Counted as `labelled_findings`, and it is the precision denominator
levels.defect_class: several claims a matcher grouped as one defect, carried on a label as `class_id`. Never counted here as a claim
levels.reading: one time an adjudicator actually read something. Counted as `readings` (distinct class_id + unbundled), and it is the only level a claim about INDEPENDENCE may use

severity_weights_source: derived from severity.mjs KNOWN's ordering, checked against spec §3.3's 4/3/2/1 at import

parse_vintage.basis: the content hash of the module whose output a CodeRabbit finding_key hashes

metrics.spec: spec §3.3 — real ÷ (real + not-real), over the findings one arm raised and an adjudicator judged

metrics.unit: summed severity weight over labelled findings
metrics.spec: spec §3.3 — Σ(weight of real claims) ÷ Σ(weight of all claims), weighted by the ANNOTATOR's severity

metrics.unit: confirmed-real findings in the cross-arm union
metrics.spec: spec §3.3 — real defects this arm found ÷ all confirmed real defects. A BAND: the union's overlap is unresolved
spec §3.3 — where the wrong claims cluster. Qualitative; every share carries its denominator and is suppressed below min_n

metrics.reason: absolute recall needs every real defect the pull request contains, INCLUDING the ones no reviewer raised — the item label's `true_defects[]`, populated from human review or a revert. The pilot corpus has none, and a set built from what reviewers found cannot contain what they missed. This is a property of the corpus, not a gap in this scorer

the miss profile describes the kinds of real defect an arm systematically misses, so it is cut over the same `true_defects[]` absolute recall needs — defects found outside both arms, which this corpus does not contain. A corpus property, not a gap in this scorer, and it does not become measurable by adjudicating more findings

refusals.reason: absolute recall needs every real defect the pull request contains, INCLUDING the ones no reviewer raised — the item label's `true_defects[]`, populated from human review or a revert. refusals.what_would_change_it: item labels carrying a non-empty true_defects[] on this corpus, sourced from outside both arms — a corpus-building task, not an adjudication one

refusals.reason: the miss profile describes the kinds of real defect an arm systematically misses, so it is cut over the same `true_defects[]` absolute recall needs — defects found outside both arms, which this corpus does not contain. refusals.what_would_change_it: the same corpus property absolute recall needs; neither becomes measurable without it

relative_recall.denominator_level: confirmed-real findings in the union of the two arms' labelled sets; the union's overlap is unresolved, so it is a band rather than a number
relative_recall.bound_basis: union_low = max(a, b) when every defect either arm confirmed the other confirmed too; union_high = a + b when the two sets are disjoint. Resolving the cross-arm pairs narrows the band; nothing here resolves them
relative_recall.reason: the coderabbit arm has no labelled finding, so the union of confirmed defects is this arm's own set and the band collapses to [1, 1] — a relative recall of 1.0 that is a property of the labelling rather than of the reviewer. Label the coderabbit arm and the denominator becomes a real one
